1567-10.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, Oct 1567 (date partly conjectural), during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Emperor says he will do his utmost for peace in Christendom; The King's ambassador to Constantinople; The ambassador sent to Constantinople; marriages of the Emperor's daughters; Portugal; He will inquire, discreetly.
1567-10.en:
⟨Madam, my last letter was of the [25th?] of last month, and since then I have not been able to speak to the Emperor until last Wednesday, for he does not leave his chamber and cannot stand on his feet.⟩

[v006r] I told him that when I took leave of you to come here, you [?commanded] me to find out whether what he had told you was true: that His Majesty, complaining of the disorders in Christendom on account of religion, [...] well that it was necessary for the Christian princes to put good order to it, and that if the others would take heed, he [?would not spare himself] on his side to take pains to bring about a good union;

1567-11-15.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 15 Nov 1567, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): News after Lignerolles left; rumour of troops levied in Germany for the Protestants.
1567-11-15.en:
[v022r] Madame, since the departure of Monsieur de Lignerolles, which was on the fifth of this month, and who went by
way of the Duke of Saxony, nothing else has happened, except that the rumour ran in this city that many foot and horse
were being raised in Germany to go to France in favour of those who have taken up arms against the King. I spoke to the
Emperor, who told me that he had been warned that men were being gathered, but that he hoped that once his mandates had
arrived no one would dare disobey, and that he would soon have news of it; that it is quite true he has been written to
that some soldiers [are going] to France by stealth from over there, but not in complete companies.

1568-01-21.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 21 Jan 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Emperor asks repeatedly for news of Lignerolles's return; He will keep the old alliances between the Empire and France.
1568-01-21.en: [v034r] [...] learn other things, except that it is decided that his children shall return to Germany as soon as possible. He has asked me several times whether there was news of the arrival of Monsieur de Lignerolles, to which I could say nothing else except that I have had no letters since the fifth of November. And as far as I can tell, I believe he wants some answer to those letters, to know how satisfied you have been with him. It seems to me that he has a real wish to keep up good friendship, and to keep him in this good opinion I [v035l] [...] to maintain this friendship, and that he will continue the ancient confederations that have been between the Empire and the kingdom of France.

1568-02-15.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the King, Vienna, 15 Feb 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Emperor is displeased at having no news since Lignerolles left; Resolution of the diet of Fulda: the Emperor to mediate with the Prince of Condé; The troubles in France and Flanders will ruin Germany; Alba levies troops in Germany.
1568-02-15.en:
[v037r] [I found him] somewhat vexed that he had had no news of you since the departure of Monsieur de Lignerolles.

[v038l] But in talking with him it seemed to me that he would be very glad if you were out of these troubles and affairs with honour, by some good [?settlement]. And indeed you will have seen, from the dispatch of [?the man] whom he sent you last Sunday, that the resolution of the diet of Fulda is to learn whether it will be your good pleasure that the Empire should mediate to reconcile the Prince of Condé and those of his following, and restore them to [your] good grace.

1568-03-06.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 6 Mar 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): Duke Johann Wilhelm of Saxony and Flacian preachers; The Emperor means to work for an end of the French civil war.
1568-03-06.en: ⟨Madam, my last letter was of the last day but one of last month, since which⟩ [f039r] I have heard that Duke Johann Wilhelm of Saxony, who has gone to France in your service, has brought with him six preachers of a sect called the Flacians, and has told them that with them and with arms he [?hopes] to chastise the papists and Huguenots; which I did not make much of, as it seemed to me he had not forces enough for such an exploit. But [...] told me one must make [?more] of it than I think, for it is only too true that he strives only to spread and increase that sect, of which his brother Duke Johann Friedrich, whom he holds prisoner, was long a member; and since then he drove them out, and the said Duke Johann Wilhelm took them in;

1568-03-27.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 27 Mar 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The marriage; the King of Spain; Grignan.
1568-03-27.en: [v049r] [...] on the subject of the marriage, he told me that [?what] he had written to you about it, it was not [his intention] to keep the matter in any delay, but that he had to wait for letters from Spain, for he did not yet know in what state the affairs of the Prince of Spain stood; and that afterwards you would see that it would not be for want of him that the marriage was not soon made. I told him that the said Sieur de Grignan was leaving well content, seeing that he could assure the King and you of the good will he bears you [and] the King, and that I hoped in God that the marriage could soon be accomplished, since the beginning was good and both parties were proceeding with good affection. And thereupon the Empress came to sup with him, which was the reason I could not hold longer discourse with him;

1568-06-04.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 4 Jun 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): No decision from Spain yet on the marriage.
1568-06-04.en:
[v065r] No occasion has ever [?arisen] to raise anything with the Emperor about the marriage, and he has said nothing to
me about it either; and as far as I can tell, he has had no resolution from Spain, without which I believe he will
hardly bring himself to conclude the marriage with the King, for the effecting of which it is said at this court that
you are sending him an ambassador.

1568-06-12.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 12 Jun 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Spanish prince's detention; the daughters' marriages; Nothing will be decided before the answer from Spain.
1568-06-12.en: [v070r] As [ϖ] (the Emperor) had told me that the Sieur [?Dietrich]stein had written to him by letters of the twelfth of last month that the King of Spain was about to send him a courier, by whom he would inform him both of the cause of the detention of the prince his son and of the decision on the rest, which concerns the marriage of his daughters. As soon as I hear that the said courier has come, I will look for an occasion to learn […] from him how he has decided to settle it. And as far as I can understand, [he has] a great wish that his eldest daughter be married soon, who on the first of November will complete nineteen years, and the second this month has completed fourteen.

1568-07-17.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 17 Jul 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): Archduke Charles to be sent to Spain for the "délivrance" of Don Carlos; The affair may take long; Archduke Charles may reside in Flanders; A courier leaves for Spain tonight.
1568-07-17.en:
[f079] […] that the lord […], the Emperor's grand [?equerry], was to go to Spain; he has not yet left, nor has any
courier, and I have not been able to learn what this long delay hangs on. Archduke Charles has come here to speak to the
Emperor, and some have tried to tell me that it is [?because of] the long delay in deciding to send [?…] there, to
[?…] earnestly [?…] the release of the prince; and that there has been some talk that Archduke Charles himself would
undertake this journey, the Emperor and the Empress having a very great wish for it, and being resolved to work with all
their power for the release of the said prince.

1568-08-14.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 14 Aug 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Emperor explains why he sends Archduke Charles to Spain; The marriage will be settled on the Archduke's return; The Duke of Bavaria's second son will go to Spain with the Archduke.
1568-08-14.en:
[f094] ⟨… in which you write to me⟩ that I should try to learn in detail what the couriers from Spain have brought,
which I have done as diligently as I could; of which, however, I have been able to learn nothing other than what I wrote
to you in my previous letters. You will have learnt from that of the [?sixth] of this month how the Emperor kept telling
me that he would speak to me. Since then he has told me that what he wanted to tell me was that he is sending his
brother Archduke Charles to Spain for two reasons: one, the affair of the Prince of Spain, and the other, the affairs of
Flanders, which seem to be in a state of great need of good provision, [?for] the good of the country, the peace of
Germany and of all Christendom;

1568-08-21.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 21 Aug 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): Passage of Archduke Charles returning from Spain; Provence; the Count of Tende.
1568-08-21.en:
[v103r] […] that he well knew you would offer the Emperor's brother, Archduke Charles, the country and passage when he
returned from Spain; and also that if by chance on his way there he touched at Marseille or some other place in
Provence, [you would] order the Count of Tende to give him the welcome and attentions that belong to such a prince. For
the Emperor loves this brother dearly, since he has always been obedient to him, and even in this last mission, in which
he showed himself very ready to do his will, […] that all the honours and pleasures done to the Archduke he will count
as done to himself. Although he has told me nothing about his brother's passage through France, I have gathered by
conjecture that if you offer it to him, he will not fail to return by that road, for the Emperor much wishes it. And
[?it is held for certain] that he will leave on the fourth of September.

1568-09-04k.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the King, Vienna, 4 Sep 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The marriage negotiation; the death of the Spanish prince; News of the prince's death; the Emperor's mourning; the King's subjects lobby German princes; The Emperor says he knows of no solicitation from France so far; The affairs of Flanders may be settled gently.
1568-09-04k.en:
[f100] [...] and said [...] that the man I had sent you had [?returned], and that you had not sent me an answer sooner, waiting until [ϖ] was quite cured, who had had fever for more than twenty days, but was well when my man left, which was the [?twenty-eighth] of last month; the fever had already left him a week before. Also that you had written to me that you found good what [he] found good, and that you were very glad that he [?remained] in this good will to complete the marriage, in which he would always find you ready, wishing that this good friendship you have together should be [...] tightened with a good alliance.

He told me that now there is no longer any difficulty in the way of the marriage being made, since the Prince of Spain was dead; but that [pp] wished to be mediator [of] this marriage, in which he could not deny of himself that he did not [...];

1568-09-04q.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 4 Sep 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The marriage; Archduke Ernst; Bohemia; The Emperor loves his eldest daughter; a good alliance would confirm the friendship; Keeping the edicts; he will find out whether the Archduke passes through France.
1568-09-04q.en:
[v109r] Since I wrote you this first letter, [the Emperor], who had promised to tell me something of his will before the
ordinary courier of Flanders left, told me that, [?] having the wish to be the mediator of this marriage as he had told
me, he thinks fit to satisfy him, and that he believes that you [?too] will find it good, for it will [?be] the better
for it; that he has resolved to send Lord Ernest […] to Spain, and for this purpose he has sent for him in Bohemia; and
that he hopes that [the King] of Spain […] the marriage, for he will write in such a way that he will see that he wishes
this marriage to be concluded as soon as it [?can]. I assured him again that I believed you would be very glad that he
[?should mediate] this marriage, and that you had no less wish than he to come to the conclusion. He told me that there
is no longer any obstacle, but [?]

1568-11-06.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 6 Nov 1568, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): Troops for the Prince of Condé; the King of Denmark; Orange; Alba.
1568-11-06.en:
[v125r] The rumour runs that Duke Wolfgang of Zweibrücken [?has gathered] some six thousand reiters and three regiments
of foot to send to the help of the Prince of Condé; and that the King of Denmark is marrying the sister of the Prince of
Orange, and that he is making a league with all the maritime towns to send help to the said Prince of Orange. I have
heard from a good source that Germany has not for a long time been as united as it is now to defend the quarrel of the
said Prince of Orange. The commissioners have continued their journey towards the Duke of Alba and the Prince of Orange;
but most people believe they will achieve nothing.

1568-12-02.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Speyer, 2 Dec 1568 (Speyer), during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Duke of Aumale; levies of reiters; Pretext of defending the Empire's lands; all to be settled on Archduke Charles's return.
1568-12-02.en:
[v129r] [The Emperor] told me that he has been written to that Monsieur d'Aumale was going to besiege a town of Duke
Wolfgang of Bavaria, and that if this was true, he feared that all the circles of the Empire would resent it and would
stir up something that might well turn to the King's harm. I [told] him that I thought that if Monsieur d'Aumale had
gone to the lands of Duke Wolfgang, what he will have done [was] to divert him, so that he should not lead into France
against [the King] the [?force] which rumour said he was assembling. He told me that he thought it very good that any
forces should be prevented from going against [the King], that good order and diligence should be used in this; but that
as for besieging lands belonging to the Empire, he fears it may give occasion to

[v130l] those who stay quiet to [make up their minds];

1569-01-14.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 14 Jan 1569, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): Courier from Madrid; the Cardinal of Guise; Barcelona and Zaragoza; the King of Portugal; The Queen of England; marriage of the Elector of Saxony's daughter.
1569-01-14.en:
[v140r] On Wednesday a courier arrived whom Archduke Charles sent from Spain, who left Madrid on the tenth of last
month. I tactfully tried to learn from [the Emperor] whether any decision had yet been taken touching the marriage. He
told me that this courier brought only news of his brother's arrival, and that […] at the beginning of the business;
but that he soon expected another, by whom he hoped to have some light; and that this courier had met the Cardinal of
Guise between Barcelona and Zaragoza. However, although I sounded him, saying that I wished the marriage to be
accomplished soon, and that I hoped, now that the Cardinal of Guise is in Spain, that everything could be concluded
without further delay, I could not draw a word more out of him on this matter. The rumour runs strongly here that [the
King of Spain] will marry the eldest daughter of [the Emperor];

1569-03-02.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 2 Mar 1569, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): News of Aumale; the King's army on the frontiers; the Archduke's return.
1569-03-02.en:
[v146r] [The Emperor] told me that he has had other news from Germany, by which [he] is informed how Monsieur d'Aumale
[has] burnt and sacked everything near Saverne, which [people] find very strange. I told him that I believe none of it, and
that this is news invented by […] who are afraid, judging by their own consciences from the offences they have done the
King; and that I am sure that the King will not allow any harm to be done to the lands of the Empire, as Monsieur de la Forest was charged to give him to understand. He told me that he has had all the reports he has received copied, to
give them to you, but I believe you will [?not be able] to have them before tomorrow; and as the ordinary
courier is leaving, I did not want to fail to inform [?you] of this. For the rest, nothing new is heard, except that the
Germans show great fear of the army that the King has on the frontiers;

1569-09-10.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the King, Vienna, 10 Sep 1569, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Cardinal of Guise in Spain; the late Queen's death; resolution on the marriage; The ambassador to send within the month; Princess Marguerite and the King of Portugal; Help from Germany; the Empress's letter; wish for an early marriage.

1569-10-01.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 1 Oct 1569 (date conjectural), during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The siege of Poitiers; Saint Martin's day.
1569-10-01.en:
[v155r] You will have been able to see fully explained, in the letter I sent you by my man whom I dispatched on
the thirteenth of last month, what you write to me in yours of the twenty-eighth of the month of August last; of which,
being unable to write anything else at present, except that I know for certain that Messieurs de Chantonnay and Vanega (Venegas) have pressed hard […] to have the marriages advanced, who however have not yet been able to settle anything, except that the
courier will be awaited whom, as I wrote to you, [the Emperor] lately sent to Spain, who cannot be back before next
Martinmas. I told [the Emperor] what you wrote to me of the state of the [?affairs] of [ϖ] (the King), at which he was very glad, especially
that your forces are together;

1569-10-15.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 15 Oct 1569 (date conjectural), during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The English ambassador; movements of troops in Germany.
1569-10-15.en:
[v161r] ⟨…⟩ except that I asked [the Emperor] to tell me whether he had learnt that anything is being negotiated [at]
the assembly being held at Erfurt that might turn to the prejudice of [ϖ] (the King). He told me that he has heard nothing more
than what he had lately told me, except that the Queen of England's ambassador is persuading the Protestant princes as
hard as he can not to abandon your enemies, and to help them, promising that she will do the same on her side; but that
he has no report that any stirring of arms is yet being made in Germany, where he has given good orders to be informed of
whatever is stirred there.

1569-10-20.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the King, Vienna, 20 Oct 1569, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): Assembly of Protestant princes and a defensive league; England's ambassador.
1569-10-20.en:
[v159r] ⟨… to this war.⟩ And since he has heard that the Protestants and several others of their
religion are holding an assembly [?at] Erfurt to negotiate a defensive league, fearing to be attacked by […] Count […]
more than by any of the others. He [says] that the Queen of England has her ambassador there, who is about to learn what is decided there, of which he has promised to inform me. He also told me that, although someone had informed him that a levy
of men was being made to go to France, there is no foundation for it; and that he has given such good orders that if there is anything he will be informed of it.

1569-10-29.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the King, Vienna, 29 Oct 1569, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): After the victory (taken to be Moncontour), the Emperor offers to mediate.
1569-10-29.en:
[f158r] ⟨…⟩ with the [?copy] of the answer you made to [the Emperor], whom I told how you were ready to leave to join
your camp, to pursue the fruit of the victory that God has given you, [?where] all the principal lords [will be] and captains of your
kingdom, with whom to take some good decision; and also about the [?offer] he made you to be willing to employ himself to
negotiate some good pacification of the present troubles; and [that] you commanded me to thank him very warmly for the
demonstration he gives of always holding in singular regard the good, profit and advantage of your kingdom, and that
[you] would answer with like affection in everything that concerns him.

1569-11-04.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, 4 Nov 1569, during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The courier; the answer; ceremonies of the marriage.
1569-11-04.en:
[v168r] I have kept back the courier in order to send you by him the answer that [ϖ] (the Emperor) will give me on what I
asked him concerning what you write to me about the ceremonies he intends to be performed at the marriage, so that you
[?may] decide to send such a person as is fitting. He told me that he will soon give me an answer and decision, and
having it I shall not fail to send it to you at once by the said courier.
